title: Get ready to be thrown into a strategic game!
content:
Literally! The first level only shows you what to do but doesn’t teach you the object and goal of the level. Despite that I quickly caught on to the concept of the game. For those who are still confused, all you need to do is to collect 10 or more of the same color tiles by placing them next to each other. 
It’s very strategic and in a way like chess, every move you make matters and you have to think 2 steps ahead in order to get that 10+ stack of the same color. It gets tricky because you get those options of stacks that have 2 or 3 colors together but I also learned to use that in my strategy as well. For example, if one of my options is 3 yellow stacked on 4 purple I can place it directly next to yellow and purple stacks. It gets even more interesting than that but I think that’s all I will write! You’ll figure it out as you play along! :)

title: Makes you think, but stingy rewards and cannot anticipate tile moves
content: Overall, I like the game – it’s very challenging to figure out a strategy to clear the boards with ever increasing complications. HOWEVER! Tiles do not move in ways that I expect, and there seems to be no pattern to which direction they move. Sometimes it’s smallest to largest pile, other times it’s largest to smallest; sometimes it’s earliest to latest, other times it’s latest to earliest. Bonuses like hammers to clear stacks, move stacks, and re-randomize colors presented, all cost coins. Or you can buy coins with real world money. The most annoying part of the game is the ads that seem to hide the skip option or put the “X”out button on the smallest tap area on the extreme limits of just barely visible to see…. Remember when you calibrated your HDR settings to make the shape just barely visible against black or white… the skip/ close buttons are on that extreme level…. I only played the game to get points for a gas rewards card in another app but I’m thinking of not playing much longer, I’m not going to pay to remove ads there are better game options available.

title: Accessibility issues
content:
Ad exit prompts are very small.  Tapping the first and end exit prompts other than in the exact center (on an iPhone) opens the App Store product page. That happens with each tap repetitively until the tap center placement is precise enough to advance.  

There is sometimes an additional middle exit prompt that is inoperably frozen on a black screen.  This seems to appear on any random ad product.

The information icon, a very small “i” in a very small circle in the  lower left corner (similarly provided by most ad agencies) does not open a reporting form for indecent/broken ads but only opens the ad agency’s privacy policy.

Other than those issues,  it is a basic color hex game. It functions smoothly and I have not encountered any bugs (in first 72 levels) While there are some small completion competitions are no actual side games. The difficulty is progressive. 

There seem to be more mandatory ads than optimal but none interrupt a game round. There are 2 optional ads for an extra hex each during the rounds.

My game app is now frozen at a center exit prompt one time too many and I am deleting.

author: the ultramind
title: Becomes impossible to progress without paying
content:
I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve lost level 220. I don’t have enough coins to “buy” any board modifiers, and it appears it is impossible to win this level without them. You’d think eventually luck of the draw would work out and if you played enough times you’d finally be able to clear the board, but no. Any time you get at all close it throws you tiles that you can’t do anything with and suddenly you’ve filled all the empty spaces. I’ve reached the limits of my frustration with this.

In general it is difficult to accumulate enough coins to buy modifiers at the frequency which the game requires them in order not to lose. Even if you sit through ads to get extra coins when you clear a level, you only get 10 instead of 5, and the good modifiers cost 50 and 100 coins each. The tile swap modifier is a complete waste of coins, it will only give different configurations of the same color groups that you already couldn’t use. Don’t waste your time with it. The hammer and the tile swap are the useful modifiers, and each use costs more coins than you will be able to earn without paying money. The only way to get larger amounts of coins is the win multiple levels in a row, and if you don’t have many coins to begin with you will never be able to do this.

Speaking of the ads, they’re obnoxious. I have never had to watch so many ads just to advance game play. You might think unlocking the free spaces would at least be a short ad, but no. You’ll sit through a long ad that you have to click through several times, it will open browser windows and the app store even though you didn’t ask it to, it will say “reward granted” and then still make you wait and tap through a couple more screens. Not all of them give you the option to mute the sound. Due to the way the ads are used to give you extra coins and spaces even if you paid for the “ad free” version you would still have to watch ads. 

This was fun at first, but they let you play and win levels just long enough to get you invested, then they make it impossible to continue without giving them your money. And the amount of coins and modifiers they offer for a $5 payment is ridiculous, you will use them up very quickly and then have to buy more. 

Don’t even get started with this one unless you have lots of money to throw at it. It could be a fun game if they made it winnable with good strategy and a little luck, but they didn’t. It’s just a money grab.

title: Fun in the beginning
content: Game was fun in the beginning but I think the developers got too ambitious before they hammered out all the bugs. Make the stack more predictable and this game could be more fun. author: Strigidae_
title: Easy at first
content: The deeper you get into the game, the game purposefully gives you unplayable stacks to fill your board causing you to lose any streak. This is more prominent when you try to compete in the event because you start winning again when you don’t have a streak going on. The game seems to try to force you to buy tools (which cost real money when you can’t advance levels). The game does a good job of making the game stacks seem random but it becomes more obvious that isn’t the case as it introduces color stacks with its top tile being a color that isn’t on the board yet. It’s not all bad, the game is great for time killing but be prepared to feel like the game is cheating you as the game progresses. I did buy the ad-free version and contrary to many reviews, I haven’t had a single ad since.
